source_notes.note: Defines sequential task learning and catastrophic forgetting; contrasts sequential learning with joint multi-task access or retaining and replaying data.
Bayesian parameter view, sequential update, diagonal-Fisher Gaussian approximation, and the EWC quadratic objective; Figure 1 compares no penalty, uniform constraint, and EWC.

The paper describes the diagonal of Fisher as the diagonal precision in its Laplace approximation and lists properties attributed to Fisher. This passage does not give a per-sample Fisher-estimation formula.

source_notes.note: Fully connected network; each task uses a fixed random pixel permutation; data are trained in shuffled mini-batches and training on a task stops after a fixed amount. Appendix describes dropout, early stopping, and hyperparameter search.

source_notes.note: Compares EWC with plain SGD, uniform L2, and dropout baselines under the stated permuted-MNIST settings; reports task retention, learning of new tasks, error growth, and Fisher overlap trends.

source_notes.note: Defines overlap using a Fréchet-distance construction on trace-normalized task Fisher matrices; the interpretation concerns shared versus distinct parameter use across tasks.

source_notes.note: Ten-game sequences are sampled from a pool of nineteen; game order can return to previous games; evaluation occurs without training; the appendix specifies repeated sets and random seeds.

The system includes EWC, a task-recognition model based on a latent-context HMM/Forget Me Not procedure, per-task replay buffers, and task-specific biases and gains. EWC is applied to games after at least 20 million frames.

source_notes.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, Figure 3A-B and adjacent §2.2 text; Figure 4 on p. 13
source_notes.note: Reports aggregate human-normalized scores across ten games, contrasts inferred and provided task labels, and shows per-game curves in the appendix. Preserve the experiment conditions when stating the result.

source_notes.locator: PDF p. 6, Figure 3C and adjacent §2.2 text
source_notes.note: In a single-game Breakout DQN perturbation test, inverse-diagonal-Fisher shaped noise was more robust than uniform noise; empirical nullspace perturbations had a similar effect to inverse-Fisher perturbations, which the authors interpret as evidence of overconfidence in low-importance estimates.

The authors report a gap from separate DQNs and identify tractable posterior/uncertainty approximation as a possible reason; the discussion names factorized Gaussian and point-estimate/diagonal-Fisher approximations as limitations.

Gives Atari preprocessing, network architecture, task-specific gain/bias transform, RL settings, task-recognition settings, and Fisher sample/multiplier settings. Table 2's printed caption says MNIST despite appearing within the Atari appendix; retain and flag this source inconsistency.
